evidence.finding: Post-incident volume averaged 5.8% above forecast and peaked 22.78% above at 10:15 and 22.37% above at 10:45.
Service level fell to 75.00% at 10:15 and 77.42% at 10:45, coinciding with the two largest demand variances.
General Service volume increased 15.27%, ASA increased 42.55%, and service level declined 4.31 points while its staffing and AHT were effectively unchanged.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in; productive staffing changed by less than one agent on average.
Independent recalculation matched every reported service-level interval exactly, rejecting a reporting error.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded during the full visible window.

primary_root_cause_detail: Intermittent unexpected demand exceeded forecast by more than 22% at 10:15 and 10:45. These were exactly the two below-target service-level intervals. The additional load was concentrated in General Service while staffing and AHT remained stable.
recommended_actions: Apply intraday overflow or cross-skilled staffing to General Service when actual demand materially exceeds forecast.
Set real-time alerts for queue-level volume variance above forecast and associated ASA growth.
Review the drivers of the localized General Service demand increase and adjust its interval forecast if the pattern recurs.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Scheduled and logged-in headcount remained at 49 throughout, with nearly unchanged productive staffing.
Aggregate AHT declined 1.35%, General Service AHT was flat, and post-start AHT averaged below forecast.
No routing event was recorded and General Service transfer rate rose only 0.18 percentage points.
No platform event occurred, and the degradation was queue-specific rather than center-wide.
Recalculated service level matched all reported intervals with zero variance.

stakeholder_summary: CC-014 was most likely caused by short demand spikes concentrated in General Service. The two service-level misses aligned exactly with volume exceeding forecast by more than 22%; staffing, AHT, routing events, platform issues, and metric error were ruled out.
